body_es: AWS Elastic Beanstalk es un servicio PaaS (Platform as a Service) que abstrae la infraestructura subyacente, permitiendo a los desarrolladores centrarse en el código de la aplicación. Beanstalk soporta múltiples plataformas: Java, .NET, Node.js, PHP, Python, Ruby, Go y Docker. Al subir el código, Beanstalk aprovisiona automáticamente los recursos necesarios: instancias EC2, grupos de Auto Scaling, balanceadores de carga, bases de datos RDS y redes. Internamente utiliza CloudFormation para gestionar el stack de infraestructura. El servicio es gratuito; solo se pagan los recursos subyacentes que se aprovisionan. Para el SAA-C03, es importante distinguir los entornos de Beanstalk: Web Server Environment para aplicaciones con tráfico HTTP entrante, y Worker Environment para procesamiento de tareas en background con SQS. Los despliegues admiten múltiples estrategias: All at Once (rápido pero con downtime), Rolling (actualiza por lotes), Rolling with additional batch (mantiene capacidad completa), Immutable (instancias nuevas antes de terminar antiguas) y Blue/Green (swap de entornos completos vía Route 53). Los archivos .ebextensions permiten personalizar la configuración del entorno mediante archivos YAML o JSON en el bundle de la aplicación. Beanstalk es ideal para equipos que priorizan velocidad de despliegue.
body_en: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) offering that automates infrastructure provisioning so developers can focus on writing code rather than managing servers. Beanstalk supports multiple runtime platforms including Java, .NET, Node.js, Python, PHP, Ruby, Go, and Docker. Uploading an application bundle triggers automatic provisioning of EC2 instances, Auto Scaling Groups, load balancers, RDS databases, and VPC networking — all managed via CloudFormation under the hood. The service itself is free; you only pay for the underlying AWS resources consumed. For the SAA-C03 exam, distinguish between the two environment tiers: Web Server Environments handle incoming HTTP/HTTPS requests via a load balancer, while Worker Environments process background tasks pulled from an SQS queue. Deployment strategies are frequently tested: All-at-Once (fastest, causes downtime), Rolling (updates batches, reduces capacity temporarily), Rolling with Additional Batch (maintains full capacity throughout), Immutable (launches new instances before terminating old ones for zero-downtime rollback safety), and Blue/Green (swaps entire environments using Route 53 weighted routing). The .ebextensions configuration directory inside the application bundle allows declarative customization of OS packages, environment variables, and AWS resource configuration.
example_code:
# Initialize Beanstalk application
eb init -p python-3.11 my-app

# Create environment and deploy
eb create my-env --instance-type t3.micro

# Deploy application
eb deploy

# View environment status
eb status
